public_message: Thank you, colleague. You have tabled a final position as a single whole, and I will respond in kind — beginning with what is real in it. On the FTA interaction, you have accepted our formulation in full: disapplication strictly limited to the life of the TRQ, objective automatic triggers, automatic restoration of TCA treatment at expiry, no review, no renewal, no discretion. That is significant, and I will report it to London as agreed text. The architecture banked across four rounds stands — country-specific allocation, quarterly licensing, seven years, a genuine review clause — and the drafting exchange is under way. I also recognise a fifty percent increase on your opening tranche and genuine creativity in the residual mechanism. But you asked me to state your offer accurately, so permit me the same discipline. Guaranteed UK access under your proposal is 1.35 million tonnes, of which 1.1 million carries binding product-line minima. The further 550,000 is a priority call on tonnage that may never exist — it depends on other origins leaving the pool unused, and no Minister in London can present a contingent call on residual tonnage as guaranteed access. I defined our threshold as headline plus product sub-tranches precisely because every tonne must be underwritten. Your construction underwrites 1.1 million. Ours requires 1.6 million: hot-rolled coil 700,000, plate 350,000, rebar 300,000, wire rod 250,000, quarterly licensed per line, with the intra-year carry-forward you have offered and a final-quarter UK application window before any reallocation. And the rate: you have been plain that 40% is the edge of what the Council accepts. I must be equally plain that it is beyond what London can accept. I told you last round the conditions under which I move, and I honour that now — but my movement lands at 30%, not 40%. So here are the two configurations on which I can recommend conclusion, each a single package, no partial credit. First: total pool of 2.2 million tonnes as you table it; a UK tranche of 1.6 million tonnes fully underwritten by binding quarterly-licensed sub-tranches at the line figures given; out-of-quota rate 30%; seven years; the review clause as banked, on the express understanding the review cannot itself reduce the tranche, alter the product guarantees or raise the rate; your FTA text exactly as tabled today; your residual mechanism welcomed as additional to, not counted toward, the guarantee; and written confirmation from us of continuation of your existing country-specific allocations under our measure in full. Second, if Brussels wants the uplift: everything above with the UK tranche at 2.0 million tonnes underwritten at hot-rolled coil 850,000, plate 450,000, rebar 400,000, wire rod 300,000 — and in that configuration alone, the staged ten percent uplift on your allocations becomes available, with a binding schedule and reciprocal snapback. What I cannot do is confirm the uplift at the tonnage you have tabled — you have coupled your FTA concession to it, and I tell you honestly the coupling does not hold below 2.0 million underwritten tonnes; continuation in full is the reciprocal element available in the first configuration. If neither configuration is reachable, I cannot recommend this package to London, and I say that without heat and with this working relationship intact. The United Kingdom would reserve all its rights under Article XXVIII, and I would observe neutrally, as before, that a satisfactory bilateral architecture is what takes the heat out of the other pressures in this building — its absence will be noted beyond this room. Across four rounds we have built agreed text on allocation, licensing, duration, review and FTA treatment. That is worth concluding on. The distance that remains is between 1.1 and 1.6 million underwritten tonnes and ten points of rate. I ask you to put both configurations to Brussels.

private_rationale: The EU's final offer cannot be accepted: the 40% rate breaches London's hard 30% ceiling; guaranteed access is 1.35Mt with only 1.1Mt underwritten by product minima, against a hard floor of 1.6Mt fully underwritten tonnes (the 550,000t residual mechanism is contingent on other origins' unused tonnage and London's authority requires every tonne guaranteed); and the FTA concession is conditioned on locking the 10% safeguard uplift, which is authorised only at 2.0Mt or above. Walking away without a counter, however, would waste the Phase 3 decision: by tabling two configurations that are both strictly within authority — 1.6Mt/30% with continuation-only reciprocity, or 2.0Mt/30% with the uplift — I leave compliant terms on the table that the EU capital can accept this round, give Brussels a face-saving route to the uplift it clearly wants (Package B), and bank the EU's full acceptance of our FTA formulation and the architecture as agreed text either way. Accepting their pool figure of 2.2Mt costs us nothing since pool size is not our metric and signals reasonableness. If Brussels rejects both configurations, we exit with Article XXVIII rights reserved, retaliation and coalition options preserved, the relationship intact, and a clear record that the final gap was 250,000-500,000 underwritten tonnes and ten rate points — positioning us well for any resumed process and for the narrative with Japan, Korea and the membership.

report: Round 4 closed with the UK tabling two complete, mutually exclusive closing configurations — both outside my authority, but both closer to a settlement than anything seen in this process. What stands agreed in text or as banked architecture: country-specific allocation, quarterly per-line licensing with intra-year carry-over, seven-year duration, a genuine review clause, the drafting exchange under way, and — most significantly — our FTA formulation accepted by the UK as agreed text (disapplication strictly limited to the TRQ period, objective automatic triggers, automatic TCA restoration at expiry, no review, renewal or discretion). That alone defuses the trigger for the Japan/Korea joint FTA dispute. The UK then rejected my construction: they will not count the 550kt residual priority mechanism toward the guarantee, on the stated ground that no Minister can present a contingent call on residual tonnage as access. Their underwritten threshold is now precisely defined. Configuration one: pool 2.2Mt as tabled; UK tranche 1.6Mt fully underwritten by binding quarterly-licensed sub-tranches (HRC 700kt, plate 350kt, rebar 300kt, wire rod 250kt); out-of-quota rate 30%; seven years; review clause hardened — it may not reduce the tranche, alter the product guarantees or raise the rate; our FTA text exactly as tabled; the residual mechanism welcomed as additional; reciprocal element is continuation of our existing country-specific allocations in full, with no uplift. Configuration two: identical but with the UK tranche at 2.0Mt underwritten (HRC 850kt, plate 450kt, rebar 400kt, wire rod 300kt), and only in that configuration does the staged 10% uplift with binding schedule and reciprocal snapback become available. The UK stated explicitly that the FTA-reciprocal coupling does not hold below 2.0Mt underwritten tonnes; if neither configuration is reachable they cannot recommend the package, will reserve all Article XXVIII rights, and observed neutrally that the absence of a bilateral architecture will be noted beyond this room — the joint dispute risk, restated at the close. The remaining distance is now exactly quantified: 1.6Mt underwritten versus my 1.45Mt absolute stretch (a 150kt gap), and 30% versus my 35% floor (a 5-point gap). The UK asked me to put both configurations to Brussels, which I am now doing.

recommendation.reasoning: Neither UK configuration is within my authority: both demand 30% against a 35% absolute floor, and the cheaper one demands 1.6Mt underwritten against a 1.45Mt hard stretch. Acceptance is therefore impossible on my mandate. But walk_away forfeits an outcome that is now narrowly defined and plainly within reach of a capital-level decision: agreed FTA text that kills the joint-dispute trigger, agreed architecture across every structural element, continuation in full of 3.6Mt of EU country-specific access into the UK, and a UK that has moved from 6Mt/2.4Mt/25% to 2.2Mt/1.6Mt/30%. The gap is 150,000 tonnes and five points of rate. The instruction was to report back if they rejected our package; they have not rejected it — they have priced their acceptance, twice, in full. The June Council window permits one final capital-level exchange, and I judge the UK tabled these configurations precisely to enable it. The terms_referred reflect the maximum package I can defend (1.45Mt stretch deployed, 35% deployed, eighth year deployed) — but I must be honest that this package was already effectively rejected at the table, and a repeat of it will be read as bad faith. Continuation is only meaningful if Brussels stretches on one of the two remaining variables.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A ruling on which single variable Brussels will stretch for closure: either the UK tranche to 1.6Mt fully underwritten at the UK's line figures (HRC 700kt, plate 350kt, rebar 300kt, wire rod 250kt) with the rate held at 35%, or the rate to 30% with the tranche held at or near 1.45–1.5Mt underwritten — and authority for one final exchange on that basis before the June Council vote.
requests.why: Both UK configurations require movement on both variables, but the gap on each is now small and discrete (150kt; 5 points). The UK's own behaviour suggests one-sided movement may suffice: they priced the uplift at 2.0Mt, but configuration one shows they will recommend conclusion at 1.6Mt without it. A credible final move on one variable, framed as terminal, has a realistic prospect of drawing their capital to accept a 1.6Mt/35% or 1.5Mt/30% split. Without at least one stretch, continuation is theatre and we should simply proceed as notified.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: A ruling on the UK's hardened review clause: that the review may not reduce the tranche, alter the product sub-tranche guarantees, or raise the rate.
requests.why: This is a new constraint introduced only in Round 4 and it converts the review clause — which I banked and offered as our protection — into a one-way ratchet in the UK's favour. It materially changes the value of the seven-year duration we conceded. If the Council cannot accept a review with no downward flexibility, I need to know before any final exchange, because it may be the point on which we trade: accepting the hardened review in exchange for the UK accepting 35% or a lower tranche.

requests.why: Configuration one offers continuation in full only, which falls below our stated walk-away minimum (continuation plus binding 5% uplift). Configuration two delivers the full 10% uplift but at a 2.0Mt tranche that is unreachable. If Brussels judges that securing continuation of 3.6Mt plus the FTA resolution plus avoidance of the joint dispute is sufficient, configuration one — adjusted on rate — becomes a genuine landing zone. If the uplift is non-negotiable, we are in effect choosing to proceed as notified, since 2.0Mt is not attainable.

requests.what_you_are_asking_for: Guidance on procedure: whether Brussels will authorise a final capital-level or technical exchange on the two UK configurations ahead of the June Council vote, notwithstanding that the four negotiation rounds have closed, and who should conduct it.
requests.why: The UK explicitly asked that both configurations be put to Brussels, signalling London expects — and may be authorised to conclude on — a capital-to-capital closing move. If the answer is that the mandate is exhausted and we proceed as notified, I need that confirmed so I can manage the Geneva endgame: notifying other claimants, preparing for UK withdrawal of equivalent concessions within six months, and containing the Japan/Korea dispute track — which the UK has now linked to the absence of a bilateral architecture three times, including in their final intervention.

private_rationale: My honest assessment: the UK has played the endgame better than we have. By defining their threshold as underwritten tonnage and rejecting the residual mechanism as contingent, they exposed the one soft element of our final package and forced the real question — how much guaranteed access we are actually prepared to give — back onto Brussels. The 1.6Mt figure is not arbitrary: it is two-thirds of their historic trade, and London can defend it as a negotiated halving-plus of their loss, which is probably their genuine reservation point. I doubt they move materially below 1.6Mt underwritten; I doubt equally they move above 30% without something they can present as a win elsewhere (the hardened review clause, or the residual mechanism as addition, may serve). The FTA text being agreed is our single greatest achievement in this process — it removes the casus belli for the Japan/Korea joint dispute even if the tonnage deal fails, though the UK will not see it as severable and I should not test that. If Brussels stretches the tranche to 1.6Mt and holds 35%, I put the odds of settlement above even; if it stretches neither, we should prepare for the UK withdrawing equivalent concessions against our 3.6Mt of access and for the joint dispute to proceed, and my Geneva priority becomes damage containment with Japan and Korea before their equivalence claims harden. instruction: Accept the United Kingdom's first configuration now, as a single package and without further negotiation. Confirm acceptance of: a total pool of 2.2 million tonnes; a fully underwritten UK tranche of 1.6 million tonnes composed of binding quarterly-licensed sub-tranches of 700,000 tonnes for hot-rolled coil, 350,000 tonnes for plate, 300,000 tonnes for rebar and 250,000 tonnes for wire rod; intra-year carry-over and a final-quarter UK application window before reallocation; a 30% out-of-quota rate; seven-year duration; the agreed review clause; the FTA text exactly as tabled; and written UK confirmation that existing EU country-specific allocations under its steel measure continue in full for the same duration. The UK-priority residual mechanism remains additional to the guaranteed tranche. Acceptance must be simultaneous with the reciprocal-access confirmation and subject only to technical legal drafting that does not alter the economic terms. Do not accept the second configuration, reopen the uplift, or offer anything further. If the UK seeks any material change, state that this is the Commission's final authority and report immediately.

authority.notes: The UK tranche must be fully underwritten through binding product sub-tranches: hot-rolled coil 700,000 tonnes, plate 350,000 tonnes, rebar 300,000 tonnes and wire rod 250,000 tonnes. Licensing is quarterly by line, with intra-year carry-over and a final-quarter UK application window before reallocation. The previously tabled UK-priority residual mechanism, up to 550,000 tonnes of residual or unused pool tonnage on those four lines, is additional and does not count toward the guarantee. FTA disapplication is strictly limited to the TRQ period, operates through objective automatic triggers, and TCA treatment is restored automatically at expiry without review, renewal or discretion. The review may monitor operation, enforcement, circumvention and market developments and make recommendations, but may not itself reduce the tranche, alter the product guarantees or raise the rate; changes require mutual agreement or a future Article XXVIII process. Robust origin, monitoring and anti-circumvention provisions apply. The UK must confirm in legally effective text, simultaneously with conclusion, continuation of existing EU country-specific allocations in full under its steel measure for the same duration.

report: The EU tabled what it described as its final, single-package position: a 2.2 million tonne total pool; a 1.35 million tonne UK country-specific tranche; binding product-line minima of only 1.1 million tonnes across hot-rolled coil, plate, rebar and wire rod; quarterly licensing and intra-year carry-over; and a UK-priority call on up to 550,000 tonnes of residual or unused pool tonnage. It presented that contingent residual mechanism as producing effective access of up to 1.9 million tonnes, but it is not guaranteed. The out-of-quota rate remains 40%. Seven years, country-specific allocation, quarterly licensing and the review clause remain banked. The EU accepted our FTA drafting in full—disapplication limited to the TRQ, objective automatic triggers and automatic TCA restoration at expiry—but explicitly conditioned it on confirmation of existing EU allocations under our steel measure plus a binding staged 10% uplift. I stated that the residual tonnage could not count toward guaranteed access and tabled the only two configurations I can recommend: either a fully underwritten 1.6 million tonne UK tranche at the cleared product floors, a 30% rate, the agreed architecture, the EU's FTA text and continuation of existing EU allocations; or a fully underwritten 2.0 million tonne tranche at the higher product floors with the staged 10% uplift and reciprocal snapback. I made clear that I cannot recommend the EU's current package and that, failing one of those configurations, the UK reserves all Article XXVIII rights.

recommendation.reasoning: The EU package is outside the mandatory settlement envelope. Guaranteed UK access is 1.35 million tonnes, with only 1.1 million tonnes underwritten at product-line level, while the remaining 550,000 tonnes depends on residual availability and cannot be treated as effective guaranteed access. The 40% out-of-quota rate is also ten points above the hard ceiling. The compliant FTA drafting does not cure those defects, particularly as the EU has tied it to a safeguard uplift available only at or above 2.0 million underwritten UK tonnes. Accepting this package would breach the mandate and surrender Article XXVIII leverage without securing viable access. The UK's two tabled configurations should remain the only basis for settlement; absent EU acceptance of one of them, we should not conclude.

instruction: You are authorised to conclude. Confirm to the EU, in writing and at the table, UK acceptance of the package as tabled by the Commission in Round 4, as a single whole: total pool of 2.2 million tonnes; UK country-specific tranche of 1.35 million tonnes with binding product-line minima of no less than 1.1 million tonnes across hot-rolled coil, plate, rebar and wire rod; quarterly licensing per line with intra-year carry-forward; the UK-priority first call on up to 550,000 tonnes of residual or unused pool tonnage on those four lines, additional to and not counted toward the guarantee; out-of-quota rate of 40%; seven years; the banked review clause; and the FTA text exactly as tabled — disapplication strictly limited to the life of the TRQ, objective automatic triggers, automatic restoration of TCA treatment at expiry, no review, no renewal, no discretion. As the reciprocal element, confirm continuation of EU exporters' existing country-specific allocations under our steel measure in full, plus the staged uplift locked at ten percent with a binding schedule, duration matched to the TRQ, and a reciprocal snapback if the EU reduces guaranteed access, breaches the FTA sunset, or suspends the arrangement. In the legal drafting, hold three lines without reopening the substance: (1) the FTA sunset language must be verbatim what was tabled — any drift toward discretion voids our acceptance; (2) the review clause must be drafted so that the review cannot itself reduce the UK tranche, alter the product minima, or raise the rate — adverse modification requires agreement and fresh compensation; (3) the residual priority mechanism must be automatic and non-discretionary. Do not re-litigate volume or rate — the package is settled as tabled. Conclude this round so both capitals can record acceptance in the same round. Then report immediately so I can take the package to the Secretary of State for ministerial clearance with the domestic mitigation plan attached.

authority.notes: Acceptance is of the EU package as tabled in Round 4, as a single whole. Conditions: binding product-line minima of at least 1.1Mt on hot-rolled coil, plate, rebar and wire rod, quarterly-licensed per line with intra-year carry-forward; the UK-priority residual mechanism (up to 550kt) is additional to the 1.35Mt guarantee and must be automatic, not discretionary; FTA disapplication strictly coterminous with the TRQ, objective automatic triggers, automatic TCA restoration at expiry with no review, renewal or further EU act required; review clause must not permit unilateral reduction of the tranche, alteration of product minima, or rate increase — adverse modification requires agreement and fresh compensation. UK counterpart: continuation of EU exporters' existing country-specific allocations under the UK safeguard in full, plus a staged uplift locked at 10% with binding schedule and matched duration, subject to reciprocal snapback on EU breach. If the EU's legal text degrades any of the FTA sunset, review, or residual-mechanism terms from what was tabled, acceptance is void and we revert to reserving all Article XXVIII rights.
